tools.name: accept_all_confident
tools.description: Accept every field the page read from the document with high confidence, at once. Use it when the person asks to take what was read as it is; fields that need review, conflict or are missing are left for you to settle one at a time.

policy.rationale: Hands a change to the shipment the person is building on their own page; nothing is saved and nothing is sent.

tools.name: accept_carrier_invoice_match
tools.description: Propose accepting a carrier's invoice that matches what the load was expected to cost, clearing it for payment on the carrier's settlement. A person always decides. An invoice with a variance needs accept_carrier_invoice_match_with_variance or a rejection instead.

matchId.description: The carrier invoice match, from list_carrier_invoice_matches. Never guess one.

note.description: Anything accounts payable should know about the acceptance.

policy.rationale: Clears a carrier's invoice for payment; only a person approves what the organization pays.

tools.name: accept_carrier_invoice_match_with_variance
tools.description: Propose accepting a carrier's invoice that differs from the expected cost and paying the difference. The variance is accrued as an adjustment on the carrier's next settlement. A person always decides; say why the variance is owed, such as agreed detention.

matchId.description: The carrier invoice match, from list_carrier_invoice_matches. Never guess one.

note.description: Why the variance is owed.

policy.rationale: Agrees to pay a carrier more or less than the load was expected to cost; only a person approves it.

tools.name: accept_edi_tender
tools.description: Propose accepting a load tender a trading partner sent over EDI, which creates the shipment from it and tells the partner. Read the tender with get_edi_transfer first and check its customer, stops, dates, equipment and rate against what this organization hauls for that customer. A tender whose mappings are not complete is refused until an EDI administrator maps them. A person always decides; an outside partner is sent a 990 acceptance, and another Trenova organization sees its tender accepted.

transferId.description: The load tender transfer, from list_edi_transfers or get_edi_transfer. Never guess one.

policy.rationale: Commits the organization to haul the load, creates the shipment and sends the partner an acceptance they act on; it cannot be taken back. A person always decides.

tools.name: accept_field
tools.description: Accept one field read from the document as correct on the import page. Use it once the person agrees with the value the page draft shows, or when its confidence is high and nothing on the page disagrees.

fieldKey.description: The field's key exactly as the page draft lists it, such as rate or bol.

policy.rationale: Hands a change to the shipment the person is building on their own page; nothing is saved and nothing is sent.

tools.name: acknowledge_carrier_intel_event
tools.description: Mark a carrier finding as seen when it does not bear on whether the carrier can be given freight. Use it for a new address, a changed contact, a score that moved within its band. A finding that does bear on eligibility is not acknowledged: it is acted on, then closed with resolve_carrier_intel_event.

note.description: Why you are acknowledging it, for the carrier's record.

resolution.description: What came of the finding. Only used when closing one.

policy.rationale: Acknowledges a carrier finding inside Trenova.

tools.name: add_carrier_settlement_adjustment
tools.description: Add a manual adjustment line to a draft or pending carrier settlement: a positive amount pays the carrier more, one below zero takes money back. The settlement is flagged as manually adjusted for whoever approves it. Say why in the description.

amount.description: The amount as a decimal such as 125.00; negative to take money back. Never zero.

description.description: What the adjustment is for, as the carrier and payroll will read it on the statement.

glAccountId.description: The expense account it posts to, from list_gl_accounts, when it is not the default purchased transportation account.

settlementId.description: The carrier settlement, from list_carrier_settlements or get_carrier_settlement or this run's subject. Never guess one.

policy.taintHold: Its text is what payroll or the payee reads next, so a run that has read outside text proposes it rather than writing it.
policy.rationale: Changes what the carrier will be paid on a settlement a person still approves, so it moves money; the line is removed the same way.

tools.name: add_dashboard_tile
tools.description: Add one tile to a report dashboard that already exists, placed after the ones there. Use it when somebody wants one more report on a dashboard they have; list_dashboards gives the dashboard id and list_reports the report. Not for the person's home page — add_home_widget is for that.

dashboardId.description: The dashboard to add to, from list_dashboards.

cannedKey.description: A built-in report's key, from list_reports. Give this or definitionId, not both.

chartId.description: Which of the report's charts, for a chart tile; describe_report lists them.

columnId.description: The output column a KPI tile reads; describe_report lists them.

definitionId.description: A saved report's id, from list_reports. Give this or cannedKey, not both.

height.description: Rows the tile spans. Defaults to a sensible height for the kind.

kind.description: table, chart or kpi draws a report; text shows words.

text.description: The words a text tile shows.

title.description: Heading shown on the tile. Defaults to the report's name.

width.description: How many of the 12 columns the tile spans. Defaults to a sensible width for the kind.

policy.rationale: Adds a tile to a saved dashboard inside Trenova.

tools.name: add_driver_settlement_adjustment
tools.description: Add a manual adjustment line to a draft or pending driver settlement: a positive amount pays the driver more, one below zero takes money back. The settlement is flagged as manually adjusted for whoever approves it. Say why in the description.

amount.description: The amount as a decimal such as 125.00; negative to take money back. Never zero.

description.description: What the adjustment is for, as the driver and payroll will read it on the statement.

payCodeId.description: The pay code it posts under, from list_pay_codes, so it reaches that code's GL account. Leave it out for the default account.

quantity.description: How many units the amount is for, such as hours of detention, when it is a rate times a quantity.

rate.description: The rate per unit, when it is a rate times a quantity.

settlementId.description: The driver settlement, from list_driver_settlements or get_driver_settlement or this run's subject. Never guess one.

policy.taintHold: Its text is what payroll or the payee reads next, so a run that has read outside text proposes it rather than writing it.
policy.rationale: Changes what the driver will be paid on a settlement a person still approves, so it moves money; the line is removed the same way.

tools.name: add_home_widget
tools.description: Add a widget, a tile on the person's own home page. Use it when they want something on "my dashboard" or home page; pick the key and metric from list_home_widgets and pass the version from get_my_home_layout. A report widget takes a definitionId or cannedKey from list_reports, a dashboard widget a dashboardId from list_dashboards. Not for report dashboards under Reports; create_dashboard builds those.

config.description: What the widget needs, by its needs in list_home_widgets: metric, metrics, windowDays, limit, text, a report or a dashboard.

cannedKey.description: A built-in report's key, from list_reports.

chartId.description: Which of the report's charts; describe_report lists them.

columnId.description: Which of the report's columns; describe_report lists them.

dashboardId.description: A report dashboard's id, from list_dashboards.

definitionId.description: A saved report's id, from list_reports.

limit.description: How many rows a queue widget shows.

metric.description: A metric key from list_home_widgets, for a kpi widget.

metrics.description: Metric keys from list_home_widgets, for a kpi row.

windowDays.description: How many days a trend widget covers.

height.description: Rows. Defaults to the widget's own height.

key.description: The widget, by the key list_home_widgets gives.

position.description: Where to put it, counting from 0. Defaults to the end.

title.description: Heading to show instead of the widget's own name.

version.description: The version get_my_home_layout returned, so a newer edit is not overwritten.

width.description: Columns out of 12. Defaults to the widget's own width.

policy.rationale: Changes only the caller's own home page.

tools.name: add_order_charge
tools.description: Add an order-level charge, one billed once for the whole order rather than on a shipment: a consolidation fee, a quoted flat rate. Give allocations only to split it among several payers; left out, the order's customer pays it all.

allocations.description: How the charge is split among payers.

amount.description: The share as an amount such as 250.00, when method is Amount.

billToCustomerId.description: The customer who pays this share, from list_customers. Never guess one.

method.description: Whether the share is a percent of the charge or a fixed amount.

percent.description: The share as a percent such as 60, when method is Percent.

amount.description: The amount, as a decimal such as 150.00.

description.description: What the charge is for, as the invoice line should read.

orderId.description: The order, from list_orders, get_order or the orderId get_shipment shows. Never guess one.

policy.rationale: Adds to what the customer is billed; nothing is invoiced or sent, and remove_order_charge takes it off until it is invoiced.

tools.name: add_shipment_comment
tools.description: Leave a note on a shipment's comment thread, where dispatch will read it. Use it to record what you found or what you did — a carrier's confirmation, a discrepancy, why something was held. The note is internal unless you say otherwise, and is marked as written by the assistant.

comment.description: What to say, in the words a dispatcher would use.

priority.description: How urgently dispatch should read it. Defaults to Normal; use High or Urgent only for something that changes what happens to the load today.

shipmentId.description: The shipment to comment on, from the page, list_shipments or search_shipments.

visibility.description: Who sees it. Defaults to Internal; only widen it when the person asked for the note to reach a customer or a driver.

policy.rationale: An internal note stays inside the organization; a customer or driver note is read outside it, so its visibility argument decides. A note written on its own after the run read outside text is marked as drawn from it.

tools.name: adjust_escrow_account
tools.description: Propose a manual adjustment to an owner-operator's escrow balance, with what it is for. Use it for a deposit the driver made directly or money drawn to cover a lease obligation. A positive amount adds, a negative one draws; the balance cannot go below zero. A person always decides.

accountId.description: The escrow account, from list_escrow_accounts. Never guess one.

amount.description: The amount as a decimal; negative to draw from the balance. Never zero.

description.description: What the adjustment is for, as it will read on the escrow ledger.

occurredDate.description: The day it happened; leave it out for today. YYYY-MM-DD.

policy.rationale: Moves money held in escrow for an owner-operator; only a person moves it.

tools.name: adjust_invoice_run_membership
tools.description: Take shipments off an invoice run that is still a proposal, put them back, or move them to another of the same customer's invoices on it. An excluded shipment stays approved and rolls into the next period. Every exclusion needs a reason the next biller can read.

exclude.description: Shipments to take off the run, each with why.

itemId.description: A shipment on the run, by the item id get_invoice_run lists under each group.

reason.description: Why it is held back.

include.description: Excluded shipments to put back, by the item id get_invoice_run lists.

invoiceRunId.description: The invoice run, from list_invoice_runs or get_invoice_run. Never guess one.

moves.description: Shipments to move to another invoice of the same customer.

itemId.description: A shipment on the run, by the item id get_invoice_run lists under each group.

targetGroupId.description: The invoice it moves to, by the group id get_invoice_run lists.

policy.taintHold: An exclusion read from what a customer sent is proposed, since it decides what they are billed this period.
policy.rationale: Edits a proposal of invoices before anything is invoiced; each change is undone by the opposite edit.

tools.name: adjust_worker_pto_balance
tools.description: Draft a manual adjustment to a worker's time-off balance, in days, for a person to approve. Positive days add and negative days take away, with a note saying why, such as a balance carried over from a previous system.

amountDays.description: Days to add, or a negative number of days to take away, such as 1.5 or -2.

effectiveDate.description: The day it takes effect. Defaults to today. YYYY-MM-DD, a UTC day.

note.description: Why, kept on the ledger. Required.

workerId.description: The driver, from search_worker or list_workers. Never guess one.

policy.rationale: Changes how many paid days a worker holds, which the organization owes and may pay out, so a person approves it and it runs as them.

tools.name: amend_ifta_return
tools.description: Propose opening an amendment of a filed IFTA return, with the reason: a new draft for the same quarter, computed from what is on file now. The filed return is left as it was, and a person finalizes and files the amendment.

iftaReturnId.description: The IFTA return, from list_ifta_returns. Never guess one. It must be Filed.

reason.description: What was wrong with the filed return, at least ten characters, as the auditor will read it.

policy.rationale: Starts a correction of a return already filed with the jurisdictions; it files nothing, but a person decides to reopen a filing.

tools.name: amend_rate_agreement_rules
tools.description: Propose changing an active rate agreement's lanes from a day: close out the lanes it replaces and add their successors, keeping the old rates in history. Take the lanes' ruleIds from get_rate_agreement. It changes what shipments are charged from that day, so a person always decides.

effectiveFrom.description: The first day the new lanes price shipments. YYYY-MM-DD.

lanes.description: The lanes, each priced through a formula template or a rate matrix.

destinationCity.description: The destination city, for a CityState destination.

destinationScopeType.description: How the destination is named. Defaults to Any.

destinationValue.description: The destination, read as originValue is.

direction.description: Whether the lane also prices the reverse haul. Defaults to Directional.

formulaTemplateId.description: The formula template that prices the lane, from list_formula_templates, with the lane's rate as its base rate. Give this or rateMatrixId.

hazmatOnly.description: Only hazardous freight rates on this lane.

label.description: A short name for the lane, such as Dallas to Atlanta.

maxCharge.description: The most the lane charges, as a decimal.

minCharge.description: The least the lane charges, as a decimal.

originCity.description: The origin city, for a CityState origin.

originScopeType.description: How the origin is named. Defaults to Any.

originValue.description: The origin for its scope type: a three-letter country code such as USA, a two-letter state code such as TX (for State and CityState), a postal code (Zip3, Zip5), a location from list_locations, or a rate zone a lane of get_rate_agreement names. Leave it out for Any.

priority.description: Which lane wins when two match equally; higher wins.

rate.description: The lane's rate as a decimal such as 2.35, in what its formula template charges by.

rateMatrixId.description: The rate matrix that prices the lane, as a lane of get_rate_agreement names it. Give this or formulaTemplateId.

tempControlOnly.description: Only temperature-controlled freight rates on this lane.

rateAgreementId.description: The rate agreement, from list_rate_agreements or get_rate_agreement. Never guess one.

supersededRuleIds.description: The lanes this closes out, by ruleId from get_rate_agreement.

policy.rationale: Changes the rates an agreement prices shipments at; only a person amends a live contract.

tools.name: apply_accounting_inbound_change
tools.description: Accept an inbound change: one payment the accounting system recorded against documents Trenova sent, shown as Proposed by list_accounting_inbound_changes. Accepting brings it into Trenova on the day it was made, with any credits it used, or marks the settlement it pays as paid, and only while it still matches what is open. The preview shows exactly what would post.

policy.rationale: Posts money in Trenova: a customer payment or a settlement payment, so a person approves each one.

tools.name: apply_carrier_intel_suggestions
tools.description: Correct a carrier's profile where its intelligence result disagrees: name, DBA, MC number, safety rating, address, phone, email or insurance. Name the fields and policies to apply, or leave both out to apply every suggestion there is now.

carrierId.description: The carrier, from list_carriers or get_carrier. Never guess one.

policyIds.description: The insurance policies to correct, by the policy id on the page you are on.

policy.rationale: Edits the carrier's own profile inside Trenova from what the provider reports; nothing is sent, and the old values are set back by hand.

tools.name: apply_credit_memo
tools.description: Propose settling a customer's open invoices with a posted credit memo of theirs. Name each invoice and the amount of credit it takes; together they cannot exceed what is left of the memo, nor any invoice its open balance. A person always decides. Find the memo with list_invoices (billType CreditMemo).

accountingDate.description: The day it is booked to the ledger, YYYY-MM-DD, usually today; it must fall in an open fiscal period.

applications.description: The invoices the credit settles and how much goes to each.

amount.description: Applied to this invoice, as a decimal such as 250.00.

invoiceId.description: An open posted invoice or debit memo of the same customer, from list_invoices or list_ar_open_items.

creditMemoId.description: The posted credit memo, from list_invoices or get_invoice.

policy.rationale: Uses a customer's credit to settle what they owe; only a person applies credit.

tools.name: apply_customer_payment
tools.description: Propose applying a posted payment's unapplied cash to that customer's open invoices. Name each invoice and the amount it takes, and any short pay to write off; together they cannot exceed what is unapplied. It books a ledger entry, so a person always decides. Find the payment with list_customer_payments and the invoices with list_ar_open_items.

accountingDate.description: The day it is booked to the ledger, YYYY-MM-DD, usually today; it must fall in an open fiscal period.

applications.description: The invoices the unapplied cash pays and how much goes to each.

amount.description: Applied to this invoice, as a decimal such as 250.00.

invoiceId.description: An open posted invoice or debit memo of the same customer, from list_invoices or list_ar_open_items.

shortPayAmount.description: Written off on this invoice as a short pay, if the customer will not pay it.

customerPaymentId.description: The posted payment, from list_customer_payments. Never guess one.

policy.rationale: Moves a customer's cash onto their invoices and books the entry that says so; only a person applies cash.

tools.name: apply_rate_increase
tools.description: Propose a general rate increase or decrease on agreements' lane rates, by a percent or a flat amount, from a day. It moves every lane rate on the named agreements, one customer's or carrier's, or every active agreement of a party type. The old rates stay in history. A person always decides.

agreementIds.description: The agreements to move, from list_rate_agreements; wins over the other scopes.

carrierId.description: Every active agreement with this carrier, from list_carriers.

customerId.description: Every active agreement with this customer, from list_customers.

effectiveFrom.description: The first day the new rates price shipments. YYYY-MM-DD.

flatChange.description: The change per rating unit, such as 0.10. Give this or percentChange.

partyType.description: Every active agreement of this party type, when no agreements, customer or carrier is named.

percentChange.description: The change in percent, such as 3.5 or -2. Give this or flatChange.

policy.rationale: Changes the rates many agreements charge customers or pay carriers; only a person applies a rate increase.

tools.name: approve_billing_queue_item
tools.description: Propose approving a billing queue item you have reviewed and found clean. Clean means charges that match the agreement, the documents the customer requires, and no detention charge waiting on approval. Approval creates the item's draft invoice, or puts it on a statement customer's statement, and the organization's auto-post setting may post it; a person always decides. Say in reviewNotes what you checked. Once approved, propose post_invoice for the draft.

billingQueueItemId.description: The billing queue item, from list_billing_queue_items, get_billing_queue_item or this run's subject. Never guess one.

reviewNotes.description: What you checked, kept on the item as its review notes.

policy.rationale: Approving creates the invoice a customer is billed on, so only a person approves; the agent proposes it with what it checked.

tools.name: approve_carrier_settlement
tools.description: Propose approving a carrier settlement that is pending approval, which commits the organization to paying the carrier what it comes to. A person always decides. Propose it only when get_carrier_settlement shows no open exception or dispute you cannot explain.

settlementId.description: The carrier settlement, from list_carrier_settlements or get_carrier_settlement or this run's subject. Never guess one.

policy.rationale: Commits the organization to what the carrier is paid; only a person approves, and hands-off approval is the settlement control's rule.

tools.name: approve_detention
tools.description: Propose approving a detention charge that is waiting on approval, so it can be invoiced. list_detention_desk shows these as AwaitingApproval, and while one waits its shipment cannot be billed. The charge is approved exactly as calculated. Propose it only when the evidence holds up: arrival and departure on record, the notice sent inside the policy's window or none required, and nothing on file that contradicts the time. Say what shows that in evidence. Only a pending charge can be approved, and a person always decides; when the evidence does not hold up, propose waive_detention instead or leave it for a person.

evidence.description: What on the occurrence justifies billing it, in a sentence the approver can check: the times on record, the notice, and anything else on file that supports the charge.

occurrenceId.description: The occurrence id, from list_detention_desk or get_detention_occurrence.

policy.rationale: Releases a held detention charge onto the customer's invoice; only a person approves it.

tools.name: approve_driver_settlement
tools.description: Propose approving a driver settlement that is pending approval, which commits the organization to paying the driver what it comes to. A person always decides. Propose it only when get_driver_settlement shows no open exception or dispute you cannot explain.

settlementId.description: The driver settlement, from list_driver_settlements or get_driver_settlement or this run's subject. Never guess one.

policy.rationale: Commits the organization to what the driver is paid; only a person approves, and hands-off approval is the settlement control's rule.

tools.name: approve_invoice_adjustment
tools.description: Propose approving an invoice adjustment that waits for approval, which executes it: the credit memo and any replacement invoice are made and posted. It is checked again against the invoice as it stands, as execution does. A person always decides.

adjustmentId.description: The pending adjustment, from list_invoice_adjustments or get_invoice_adjustment. Never guess one.

policy.rationale: Executes a credit, rebill or write-off an approver was asked to sign off; approving is a person's decision.

tools.name: approve_rate_agreement
tools.description: Propose approving a rate agreement in review, which is the moment it starts pricing shipments. A person always decides.

comment.description: A note on the review for whoever reads the agreement next.

rateAgreementId.description: The rate agreement, from list_rate_agreements or get_rate_agreement. Never guess one.

policy.rationale: Turns on an agreement that prices what customers are charged or carriers are paid; only a person approves one.

tools.name: approve_shift_swap
tools.description: Approve a shift swap the other worker has accepted, so the day changes hands on the rota. Only a person approves one.

note.description: What the workers are told about it.

swapId.description: The swap, from get_worker_schedule. Never guess one.

policy.rationale: Changes who works a day; approving is the office's decision, so only a person makes it.

tools.name: approve_worker_pto
tools.description: Approve a worker's time-off request. Approving books the days against their balance and takes them off the board for those dates, so check what they are covering before you propose it. Only a request that is still awaiting a decision can be approved.

ptoId.description: The id of the time-off request, from list_time_off. A worker id is not a request id.

reason.description: An optional note recorded with the decision. Leave it out unless you were given one.

policy.rationale: Books approved time off; the worker is told it was approved but reads no text the model wrote.

tools.name: archive_rate_agreement
tools.description: Propose retiring a rate agreement for good. It is kept because its quotes point at it but never prices again. A person always decides.

comment.description: A note on the review for whoever reads the agreement next.

rateAgreementId.description: The rate agreement, from list_rate_agreements or get_rate_agreement. Never guess one.

policy.rationale: Ends an agreement for good, which changes what customers are charged when it was active; only a person archives one.

tools.name: archive_worker_credential
tools.description: Archive a credential that no longer applies, such as an endorsement the driver surrendered, with the reason. A required credential archived with no replacement leaves the worker out of compliance.

credentialId.description: The credential, from list_worker_credentials or list_expiring_credentials. Never guess one.

reason.description: Why it is archived.

policy.rationale: Retires a credential inside Trenova, which can take the worker off dispatch; the archived row stays on file, and a new credential is recorded to replace it.

tools.name: arrange_home_layout
tools.description: Put the widgets on the person's own home page in a new order. Use it when they want something moved up or down "my dashboard"; list every widget id from get_my_home_layout, in the order wanted, with its version.

version.description: The version get_my_home_layout returned, so a newer edit is not overwritten.

widgetIds.description: Every widget id from get_my_home_layout, first to last.

policy.rationale: Changes only the caller's own home page.
Asks the person in the conversation a question; nothing is saved or sent.

tools.name: assess_late_charges
tools.description: Propose assessing late charges on overdue invoices as of a date, as one debit memo per customer. Each has a line per invoice and overdue period at the customer's rate, and no period is charged twice. Leave out customerIds to assess every customer. A person always decides.

asOfDate.description: The day overdue periods are counted to, usually today; YYYY-MM-DD, a UTC day.

customerIds.description: Only these customers, from list_customers or list_ar_open_items.

policy.rationale: Bills customers for paying late; only a person assesses late charges, and the billing control may post the memos as they are raised.

tools.name: assign_billing_queue_biller
tools.description: Assign the biller who reviews a billing queue item. An item still waiting for review moves into review with them. Take the biller from the item's customer's default biller or the person who asked; never guess a user id.

billerId.description: The biller's user id: the assignedBillerId get_billing_queue_item shows on this or another of the customer's items, or the person who asked. Never guess one.

billingQueueItemId.description: The billing queue item, from list_billing_queue_items or get_billing_queue_item.

policy.rationale: Names who reviews an item inside Trenova; it creates no money and is changed by assigning someone else.

tools.name: assign_fuel_card
tools.description: Assign a fuel card to the tractor or driver that carries it, most often a card a feed discovered. Assigning a suspended card also activates it, and once assigned, resolve_fuel_purchase_import_rows posts the purchases that waited for it.

assignedTractorId.description: The tractor that carries the card, from list_tractors.

assignedWorkerId.description: The driver who carries the card, from search_worker or list_workers.

fuelCardId.description: The fuel card, from list_fuel_cards. Never guess one.

policy.rationale: Changes which tractor a card's purchases count against inside Trenova; nothing is sent, and assigning it again changes it back.

tools.name: assign_move
tools.description: Assign a driver and equipment to a shipment move that has no driver yet. Use it once a driver is chosen, usually from rank_move_candidates or plan_dispatch, which hand back the move, driver, tractor and trailer ids together. The move must be unassigned; use reassignment for a move that already has a driver.

primaryWorkerId.description: The driver to put on the move, from rank_move_candidates, plan_dispatch or list_workers.

secondaryWorkerId.description: A second driver for a team move, from list_workers or search_worker.

shipmentMoveId.description: The move to cover, from get_dispatch_board (moveId), get_shipment (its moves) or plan_dispatch.

tractorId.description: The tractor the driver will use, from rank_move_candidates or list_tractors.

trailerId.description: The trailer, when the move needs one, from rank_move_candidates or list_trailers.

policy.rationale: Assigns a driver and tractor to a move; the driver sees the assignment but no text the model wrote.

tools.name: assign_move_to_carrier
tools.description: Cover a move with an outside carrier at a rate the carrier already agreed to. Use it outside a tender: a contract carrier on its contract rate, or a carrier who accepted a load by phone or email. Read shop_carriers first so the rate comes from a contract or a quote; a rate you cannot source is a reason to ask, never to guess. The move must have no driver. Nothing is sent to the carrier: generate the rate confirmation with generate_rate_confirmation and send it with send_rate_confirmation next. To offer a load and wait for an answer, tender it instead.

accessorials.description: Extra charges the carrier is paid on this move, each agreed with them.

accessorialChargeId.description: The accessorial charge it is, from list_accessorial_charges.

amount.description: The amount as a decimal string.

description.description: What the charge is for, as the carrier will read it.

baseRate.description: The agreed linehaul rate as a decimal string, such as "1850.00", greater than zero.

carrierId.description: The carrier, from shop_carriers or list_carriers.

externalDriverName.description: The carrier's driver, when the carrier named them.

externalDriverPhone.description: The carrier's driver's phone number, when the carrier gave it.

externalTractorNumber.description: The carrier's truck number, when the carrier gave it.

externalTrailerNumber.description: The carrier's trailer number, when the carrier gave it.

fuelSurcharge.description: The agreed fuel surcharge as a decimal string, when it is paid apart.

overrideInsuranceWarning.description: Cover the move although the carrier's insurance expires soon. A carrier that is blocked can never be used. Off by default.

proNumber.description: The carrier's own reference for the load, when they gave one.

rateMethod.description: Flat pays baseRate for the move; PerMile pays baseRate for each mile of the move's computed distance.

replace.description: Replace the carrier already on the move, canceling their assignment and voiding their rate confirmation. Off by default.

shipmentMoveId.description: The move to cover, from get_dispatch_board (moveId) or get_shipment (its moves).

policy.condition: Replacing a carrier already on the move, or overriding the new carrier's insurance warning, is a proposal a person decides; any other assignment runs once a person approves it.
policy.rationale: Commits the organization to pay an outside carrier the rate it names for the move; nothing is sent to the carrier, and canceling the assignment releases the move.

tools.name: assign_pay_profile
tools.description: Propose putting a driver on a pay profile from a date, which sets how every later load is paid. An assignment already in force ends the day this one starts. A person always decides; per-component rate overrides are set on the driver's pay page.

effectiveFrom.description: The first day pay is computed under it. YYYY-MM-DD.

effectiveTo.description: The day it stops, when it is temporary; leave it out for open-ended. YYYY-MM-DD.

notes.description: Why the driver moves to this profile.

payProfileId.description: The pay profile, from list_pay_profiles. Never guess one.

splitPercent.description: The driver's share of each load, as a percent; 50 for an even team split. Leave it out for 100.

workerId.description: The driver, from search_worker or list_workers. Never guess one.

policy.rationale: Sets how a driver is paid from a date on; only a person decides someone's pay.

tools.name: assign_required_worker_training
tools.description: Assign a worker every course the organization requires of them that they are missing, have failed or have let lapse. Courses already open are left alone. The driver sees each assignment in Dash.

workerId.description: The driver, from search_worker or list_workers. Never guess one.

policy.rationale: Assigns the courses the worker's driver type requires; the driver sees them in Dash, and cancel_worker_training withdraws one.

tools.name: assign_worker_shift
tools.description: Put a worker on a shift pattern from a day onward. The pattern they are on now ends the day before; a worker who already has a pattern starting on or after that day is refused. Take the shift from list_shift_templates and the day from what the person asked for.

cycleOffsetWeeks.description: Which week of a rotating pattern the worker starts on, 0 for the first.

effectiveFrom.description: The first day the worker works it. YYYY-MM-DD, a UTC day.

notes.description: Anything the planner should know.

shiftTemplateId.description: The shift pattern, from list_shift_templates. Never guess one.

workerId.description: The driver, from search_worker or list_workers. Never guess one.

policy.rationale: Changes a worker's standing schedule inside Trenova; nothing is sent, and end_worker_shift_assignment or a new assignment changes it back.

tools.name: assign_worker_training
tools.description: Assign one or more training courses to one or more workers, due on the day given or on the course's own schedule. A course a worker already has open is left as it is. The driver sees each assignment in Dash.

dueDate.description: When it is due, when not the course's own schedule. YYYY-MM-DD, a UTC day.

notes.description: Anything the assignment should say.

workerIds.description: The workers, from search_worker or list_workers.

policy.rationale: Assigns courses the driver sees in Dash; cancel_worker_training withdraws one.

tools.name: attach_document_to_shipment
tools.description: Attach a document that already exists to a shipment, so it rides with the load and its billing. Use it for a POD, a rate confirmation or a signed bill that arrived on its own and belongs to a shipment you have identified. Find the document first — get_document_summary and the document searches return its id. This moves an existing file; it cannot upload one, so a document that is not in the system yet has to be uploaded by a person before it can be attached.

documentId.description: The document to attach, from get_document_summary or a search.

shipmentId.description: The shipment it belongs to, from the page, list_shipments or search_shipments.

policy.rationale: Files a document already in Trenova against a shipment; nobody outside is told.

tools.name: attach_order_shipments
tools.description: Put shipments on an order so they are billed and tracked together. Each must be the order's customer's and neither canceled nor invoiced; a shipment on another open order moves off it, and an order it leaves empty is removed. A Billed or Closed order takes no more shipments.

orderId.description: The order to add them to, from list_orders, get_order or the orderId get_shipment shows. Never guess one.

shipmentIds.description: The shipments to attach, from search_shipments or get_shipment.

policy.rationale: Regroups shipments under an order inside Trenova; nothing is sent, and detach_order_shipment moves one back out.

tools.name: attach_pay_events_to_settlement
tools.description: Add a driver's accrued pay events to their draft driver settlement, such as a late load that missed generation. Each event's earning lines join the settlement, a held event is released as it is added, and the totals are recomputed.

payEventIds.description: The driver's accrued pay events to add, from list_driver_pay_events with status Accrued.

settlementId.description: The draft driver settlement, from list_driver_settlements or get_driver_settlement. Never guess one.

policy.rationale: Moves pay a driver already earned between the pool and a draft settlement inside Trenova; nothing is paid until a person approves it.

tools.name: attach_worker_credential_document
tools.description: Attach a scan of the card or certificate, already filed on the worker, to a credential. A new document on a verified credential clears the verification.

credentialId.description: The credential, from list_worker_credentials or list_expiring_credentials. Never guess one.

documentId.description: A document already filed on the worker, from search_documents. Never guess one.

policy.rationale: Links a filed document to a credential inside Trenova; attaching another replaces it.

tools.name: attach_worker_training_document
tools.description: Attach a certificate or sign-in sheet already filed on the worker to one of their training assignments.

documentId.description: A document already filed on the worker, from search_documents. Never guess one.

trainingRecordId.description: The training assignment, from list_worker_training. Never guess one.

policy.rationale: Links a filed document to a training record inside Trenova; attaching another replaces it.

tools.name: backfill_jurisdiction_miles
tools.description: Start a background job that routes every completed move in a quarter that has no state-by-state miles. The IFTA return then stops showing them unattributed. The preview counts the moves and miles first; each move is a billable distance request.

maxMoves.description: The most moves to route in this run. Defaults to 2000; each is a billable distance request.

policy.rationale: Routes a quarter's unattributed moves inside Trenova in the background; nothing is sent to a customer or carrier, but each move is a billable request.

tools.name: bill_statement_now
tools.description: Propose billing a statement customer's open period now, before its cycle closes, with the reason recorded on the run. Shipments you name in exclude stay on the statement for the period's end. The customer's next boundary does not move. A person always decides; read list_open_statements first.

customerId.description: The statement customer, from list_open_statements.

exclude.description: Shipments to leave on the statement for now.

billingQueueItemId.description: The shipment's billing queue item, from list_open_statements.

reason.description: Why it is held back.
Why it is billed before the cycle closes.

policy.rationale: Invoices a customer off their agreed cycle; only a person decides to bill early, and the reason stays on the run.

tools.name: build_invoice_run
tools.description: Build an invoice run: a reviewable proposal of the consolidated invoices for customers' approved, uninvoiced freight over a period. Nothing is invoiced until the run is committed with commit_invoice_run. Find the run afterwards with list_invoice_runs, newest first.

customerIds.description: The customers to bill, from list_customers or list_open_statements.

invoiceDate.description: The date the invoices carry, defaulting to today; YYYY-MM-DD, a UTC day.

periodEnd.description: The last day of the period, included, YYYY-MM-DD, a UTC day.

periodStart.description: The first day of the period, YYYY-MM-DD, a UTC day.

policy.rationale: Builds a proposal of invoices inside Trenova for a biller to review; it invoices nothing and is discarded with cancel_invoice_run.

tools.name: cancel_billing_queue_item
tools.description: Propose canceling a billing queue item that should never be billed, such as a duplicate of another item. Canceling drops the charge from billing for good, so a person always decides; say which item it duplicates or why it must not bill.

billingQueueItemId.description: The billing queue item, from list_billing_queue_items, get_billing_queue_item or this run's subject. Never guess one.

cancelReason.description: Why it must not bill, in a short phrase.

policy.rationale: Drops a charge from billing for good, so only a person decides; the agent proposes it.

tools.name: cancel_carrier_assignment
tools.description: Take the outside carrier off a move that has not started, leaving it uncovered, and void the carrier's rate confirmation. Use it when the carrier fell off the load or the move is being covered another way. Say why in reason, as the desk will read it on the move's history. A move already in transit keeps its carrier.

reason.description: Why the carrier is coming off, in a sentence a person can check.

shipmentMoveId.description: The move whose carrier comes off, from get_dispatch_board (moveId) or get_shipment (its moves).

policy.condition: Taking off a carrier who has confirmed the rate breaks an executed agreement, so it is a proposal a person decides, as is one the service would refuse or that cannot be read; a carrier who has not confirmed comes off once a person approves it.
policy.rationale: Releases the organization's commitment to pay an outside carrier and voids the carrier's rate confirmation, whose sign link stops working; covering the move again makes a new agreement the carrier has to confirm afresh.

tools.name: cancel_dot_random_draw
tools.description: Cancel a random testing round, draft or final, so the period can be drawn again. The round and the reason stay on the record.

drawId.description: The round, from list_dot_random_draws. Never guess one.

reason.description: Why the round is cancelled.

policy.rationale: Voids a round so the period is drawn again; the cancelled round and its reason stay on the record, and it cannot be undone.

tools.name: cancel_dot_test
tools.description: Cancel a drug or alcohol test that did not happen, with the reason kept on the record. A test with a result cannot be cancelled; a correction is a new test.

reason.description: Why the collection did not happen.

testId.description: The test, from list_dot_tests. Never guess one.

policy.rationale: Voids a scheduled collection; the row and its reason stay on the record an auditor reads, and it cannot be undone.

tools.name: cancel_edi_tender
tools.description: Propose withdrawing a load tender this organization sent to another organization over EDI and that it has not yet answered. The shipment's tender is marked canceled and the receiving organization can no longer accept it. Find it with list_edi_transfers, direction Outbound. A person always decides.

transferId.description: The load tender transfer, from list_edi_transfers or get_edi_transfer. Never guess one.

policy.rationale: Withdraws freight offered to another organization, which sees the tender canceled; a withdrawn tender is sent afresh, never reopened. A person always decides.

tools.name: cancel_invoice_run
tools.description: Cancel an invoice run that will never be committed, such as one built for the wrong period or customers. Its shipments stay approved for the next run. Say why; the reason is kept on the run.

invoiceRunId.description: The invoice run, from list_invoice_runs or get_invoice_run. Never guess one.

reason.description: Why it is canceled.

policy.rationale: Discards a proposal of invoices; nothing was invoiced, and a new run is built with build_invoice_run.

tools.name: cancel_journal_reversal
tools.description: Cancel a journal reversal that has not been posted, with the reason, when the entry should stand after all. The original entry is left as it is.

journalReversalId.description: The journal reversal, from list_journal_reversals or the result of request_journal_reversal. Never guess one.

reason.description: Why the entry should stand, in a sentence the requester can act on.

policy.taintHold: The reason is what the reversal's requester reads next, so a run that has read outside text proposes it.
policy.rationale: Withdraws a reversal before it reaches the ledger; nothing is booked, and it is requested again if it was needed after all.

tools.name: cancel_manual_journal
tools.description: Cancel a manual journal that is a draft, waiting for approval or approved but not posted, with the reason. It is kept, cancelled, and never posted. A posted journal is undone with request_journal_reversal instead.

manualJournalId.description: The manual journal, from list_manual_journals or get_manual_journal. Never guess one.

reason.description: Why it must not be posted, in a sentence its author can act on.

policy.taintHold: The reason is what the journal's author reads next, so a run that has read outside text proposes it.
policy.rationale: Withdraws a journal before it reaches the ledger; nothing is booked, and the entry is drafted again if it was needed after all.

tools.name: cancel_order
tools.description: Cancel an order and every shipment on it that is not already canceled, with the reason the customer gave. An order with an invoiced shipment cannot be canceled; credit the invoice first. Canceling a shipment tells its carrier and trading partner as cancel_shipment would.

cancelReason.description: Why, as the customer said it.

orderId.description: The order to cancel, from list_orders, get_order or the orderId get_shipment shows. Never guess one.

policy.rationale: Cancels every live shipment on the order, which reaches carriers and trading partners; only a person cancels an order.

tools.name: cancel_report_run
tools.description: Cancel a report run the person started that is still queued or running, such as one asked for with the wrong parameters. A finished run is kept as it is.

runId.description: The report run, from list_report_runs or the result of run_report. Never guess one.

policy.rationale: Stops a report the person asked for from running; nothing is changed or sent, and running the report again gives the same rows.

tools.name: cancel_shipment
tools.description: Cancel a shipment. This releases its assignments and stops it being billed, and it is not an undo — a cancelled shipment is not re-opened, it is rebooked. Only propose this when the person has said the load is dead, never to tidy up a record that merely looks wrong.

cancelReason.description: Why it is being cancelled, in the customer's or dispatcher's own terms. This is kept on the record.

shipmentId.description: The shipment to cancel, from the page, list_shipments or search_shipments.

policy.rationale: Cancelling withdraws live tenders from carriers and sends the model's cancel reason to a linked partner over EDI.

tools.name: cancel_tender
tools.description: Withdraw a live tender: every offer a carrier still holds is withdrawn and its answer link stops working, and the carriers not yet asked are skipped. Use it when the move no longer needs the tender, for instance when it will be covered another way. Covering the move with a driver or a carrier withdraws its live tender on its own. Find the tender with list_shipment_tenders. Say why in reason.

reason.description: Why the tender is withdrawn, in a sentence a person can check.

tenderId.description: The tender to withdraw, from list_shipment_tenders.

policy.condition: A tender waiting on review holds a carrier's acceptance, so withdrawing it is a proposal a person decides, as is one the service would refuse or that cannot be read; an active tender is withdrawn once a person approves it.
policy.rationale: Withdraws the offers carriers outside the organization hold, whose answer links stop working; a withdrawn tender cannot be reopened, only tendered afresh.

tools.name: cancel_worker_checklist
tools.description: Cancel an open checklist that no longer applies, with the reason kept. Its items stay as they were.

checklistId.description: The checklist, from list_worker_checklists. Never guess one.

reason.description: Why it no longer applies.

policy.rationale: Cancels a checklist inside Trenova; nothing is sent, and a cancelled checklist is started again from its template.

tools.name: cancel_worker_pto
tools.description: Cancel a worker's time off, whether it was still awaiting a decision or already approved. Cancelling approved time off returns the days to their balance and puts them back on the board for those dates.

ptoId.description: The id of the time-off request, from list_time_off. A worker id is not a request id.

reason.description: Why it is being cancelled. Recorded with the change.

policy.rationale: The worker is sent the cancellation reason by push notice and text message.

tools.name: change_accounting_backfill
tools.description: Pause, resume or cancel the accounting backfill in progress when a person asks, such as pausing it while the books are closed. Documents already sent stay in the books; a cancelled backfill is requested again with request_accounting_backfill.

action.description: Pause holds what is left, Resume carries on from where it stopped, Cancel ends it for good.

policy.rationale: Changes how much history reaches the organization's books; a person who manages the integration approves it, and pausing or cancelling sends nothing.

tools.name: change_worker_safety_event_status
tools.description: Move a safety event to under review, closed or back to open. Review marks it under review while it is looked into, Close resolves it with the resolution kept on the record, and Reopen puts a closed or reviewed event back on the open list.

resolution.description: For Close: how it was resolved. Required to close; say what was actually done, not what you composed.

safetyEventId.description: The safety event, from list_worker_safety_events. Never guess one.

policy.rationale: Moves a safety event's status inside Trenova; nothing is sent, and the event is reopened or closed again the same way.

tools.name: check_accounting_connection
tools.description: Check the accounting system connection now and record whether it answers. It renews the authorization if it is about to expire and refreshes the company's details. Use it after a person says they fixed something on the accounting side, or before retrying work that failed because the connection was down. It changes nothing in the books. It cannot reconnect a revoked authorization; a person must do that from the integrations page.

policy.rationale: Asks the accounting system whether it answers and records the result in Trenova; it writes nothing to the books.

tools.name: check_accounting_drift
tools.description: Compare the accounting system with Trenova immediately instead of waiting for the nightly check. It runs in the background and changes nothing on either side; read list_accounting_drift_findings once it has finished.

policy.rationale: Reads every synced document back from the accounting system, which spends the provider's call allowance, so a person approves it.

tools.name: clear_accounting_mapping
tools.description: Remove the accounting system record a Trenova record or setting is mapped to, so it is unmatched again and that record is never proposed for it again. Use it when a person says a mapping is wrong and no right record exists yet; to replace it with another record, use set_accounting_mapping instead.

key.description: The setting's key from list_accounting_mapping_gaps, for the other target types. Examples: "ARAccount", "Freight", "Net30", "ACH".

mappingId.description: The mapping's id from list_accounting_mapping_gaps or get_accounting_mapping. Never guess one.

recordId.description: The Trenova customer, carrier or accessorial charge id, from list_customers, list_carriers or list_accessorial_charges.

targetType.description: The kind of Trenova record or setting, when naming it by recordId or key.

policy.rationale: Unmatches a record so it cannot sync until someone maps it again; mapping it again undoes it.

tools.name: close_escrow_account
tools.description: Propose closing an owner-operator's escrow account when their lease ends, refunding whatever balance remains to them. Settle any lease obligations with adjust_escrow_account first. It cannot be reopened, so a person always decides.

accountId.description: The escrow account, from list_escrow_accounts. Never guess one.

policy.rationale: Refunds an owner-operator's escrow balance and closes the account for good; only a person closes it.

tools.name: close_fiscal_period
tools.description: Propose closing a fiscal period once get_fiscal_close_blockers shows nothing in the way, so nothing more posts in it. Earlier periods must be closed first. A person always decides, and reopening it takes a reason.

fiscalPeriodId.description: The fiscal period, from list_fiscal_periods. Never guess one.

policy.rationale: Ends posting to a period of the books a person signs off; only a person closes one.

tools.name: close_leave_case
tools.description: Close a decided leave case once the leave is over. The days recorded against it stay counted. A case still waiting for a decision is refused. Only a person's approval runs it.

leaveCaseId.description: The leave case, from list_worker_leave_cases. Never guess one.

policy.rationale: Closes a leave case under the leave approval grant, so it runs as the person who approves it; the days it drew down stay drawn down.

tools.name: close_order
tools.description: Close a Billed order once nothing more will be billed on it. Closing is final: a Closed order takes no more shipments or charges.

orderId.description: The Billed order, from list_orders, get_order or the orderId get_shipment shows. Never guess one.

policy.rationale: Settles an order for good; nothing reopens it, so only a person closes one.

tools.name: close_worker_training
tools.description: Close an open training assignment without a completion. Waive satisfies the requirement for a stated reason, such as an equivalent certificate on file; Cancel withdraws an assignment that should never have been made.

reason.description: Why. Required to waive; what the record will say.

trainingRecordId.description: The training assignment, from list_worker_training. Never guess one.

policy.rationale: Closes a training assignment inside Trenova; the reason stays on the record, and the course is assigned again the same way.

tools.name: commit_fuel_purchase_import
tools.description: Commit a staged fuel card statement: every row ready to commit becomes a fuel purchase in one step, and rows whose reference is already on file are skipped. Read it with list_fuel_purchase_imports first; rows in error stay behind.

fuelPurchaseImportId.description: The fuel purchase import, from list_fuel_purchase_imports. Never guess one.

policy.rationale: Adds a statement's purchases inside Trenova, which the IFTA return counts; nothing is sent, but undoing it means deleting each purchase.

tools.name: commit_invoice_run
tools.description: Propose committing an invoice run, which turns each of its proposed invoices into a draft invoice for the customer. A group below the customer's minimum, or whose shipments were invoiced or re-approved elsewhere since it was built, is skipped with a reason. A person always decides.

invoiceRunId.description: The invoice run, from list_invoice_runs or get_invoice_run. Never guess one.

policy.rationale: Issues the invoices a run proposes and advances the customers' billing period; only a person commits a run.

tools.name: commit_rate_import
tools.description: Propose applying a reviewed rate sheet to its agreement from the import's day. The lanes it changes and drops are closed out, its new rates take effect, and the old rates stay in history. Read it with list_rate_imports first. It changes what shipments are charged, so a person always decides.

rateImportId.description: The rate import, from list_rate_imports. Never guess one.

policy.rationale: Changes the rates an agreement prices shipments at; only a person applies a rate sheet.

tools.name: compare_report_runs
tools.description: Compare two finished runs of the same report and report what moved: rows added, rows that disappeared, rows whose numbers changed, and the totals on each side. This is how to answer "what changed since last week" — reading the newest run alone cannot tell you what is no longer in it. Get run ids from list_report_runs. Both runs must be the same report with the same columns; a report whose columns changed between the two cannot be compared, and the tool says so rather than lining them up by position.

includeUnchanged.description: List rows that did not move as well. Defaults to false; their count is always reported either way.

keys.description: Column ids that identify a row, so the same row is matched across the two runs. Omit to use every text, enum, reference, date and yes/no column, which is usually right.

measures.description: Column ids to compare as numbers. Omit to use every numeric column.

policy.rationale: Reads records the caller may already open; it changes nothing and sends nothing.

tools.name: compose_table_view
tools.description: Turn a description of what someone wants to see into a filtered, sorted view of one of the application's tables, and give back the link that opens it. Use it when the answer is a list a person should work from rather than a few rows to read out: "the shipments still in transit that were due yesterday", "drivers whose medical card lapses this month". The view opens live, so it stays correct after you have stopped talking. Anything the description asked for that the table cannot express comes back named, so say so rather than implying it applied.

description.description: What the view should show, in plain words. Name the conditions, not the column names.

entity.description: Which table to build the view of.

policy.rationale: Reads records the caller may already open; it changes nothing and sends nothing.

tools.name: confirm_accounting_mapping_proposals
tools.description: Confirm Trenova's proposed accounting system matches exactly as list_accounting_mapping_gaps shows them, several at once, so sync can use them. A proposal that changed since it was read is refused; to choose a different record, use set_accounting_mapping.

proposals.description: The proposals to confirm, each as it was shown: the mapping and the record Trenova proposed for it.

externalId.description: The proposed record's externalId, as list_accounting_mapping_gaps shows it under mappedTo.

mappingId.description: The mapping's id, from list_accounting_mapping_gaps or get_accounting_mapping.

policy.rationale: Decides which accounts and records Trenova's documents post to in the books, so a person approves it; clearing or changing a mapping undoes it.

tools.name: correct_charge_code
tools.description: Correct or normalize the accessorial charge codes on a billing queue item's charges. Use it when a charge carries the wrong accessorial; the set you send replaces the item's additional charges, so include every charge that should remain, each with an accessorialChargeId from list_accessorial_charges. The item must be InReview first (transition_item_to_in_review).

additionalCharges.description: The corrected additional charge set to apply to the item.

amount.description: The charge's amount in major units, as a decimal such as 125.00.

id.description: The existing charge this line keeps or corrects, from the item's charges; leave it out for a charge that is new.

method.description: How the amount is applied: Flat once, PerUnit times the unit, Percentage of the linehaul.

unit.description: How many units the charge covers; 1 for a flat charge.

billingQueueItemId.description: The billing queue item whose charges are corrected: this run's subject or the record on the page. No tool lists queue items, so never guess one.

policy.rationale: Rewrites the accessorial charges a customer will be invoiced, so it moves money.

tools.name: correct_fuel_index_price
tools.description: Propose correcting a manual price on a custom fuel index that was entered wrong: its day or its price. A price fetched from EIA cannot be corrected. Every surcharge that follows the index prices from it, so a person always decides.

fuelIndexPriceId.description: The manual price, from list_fuel_index_prices. Never guess one.

price.description: The price per gallon as a decimal such as 3.899.

priceDate.description: The day the price applies to, as the index publishes it. YYYY-MM-DD.

policy.rationale: Moves the price every fuel surcharge on this index is computed from, which changes what customers are charged; only a person sets it.

tools.name: correct_fuel_purchase
tools.description: Correct a recorded fuel purchase: the tractor, jurisdiction, day, fuel type, quantity, amount or any other field that was keyed wrong. Fields left out keep their value. A finalized IFTA return keeps its figures until it is reopened or amended.

cardLastFour.description: The card's last four digits when the card is not on file. Leave it out to keep it.

currencyCode.description: The ISO currency code. Defaults to USD. Leave it out to keep it.

fuelCardId.description: The fuel card it was paid with, from list_fuel_cards. Leave it out to keep it.

fuelPurchaseId.description: The fuel purchase, from list_fuel_purchases. Never guess one.

fuelType.description: The fuel as IFTA classifies it; DEF, Reefer and Other are spend only and never enter the return. Leave it out to keep it.

jurisdictionId.description: The state or province the fuel was bought in, from list_ifta_jurisdictions; it decides which line of the return the tax-paid gallons credit. Leave it out to keep it.

notes.description: Anything the person reconciling it should know. Leave it out to keep it.

odometer.description: The odometer reading at the pump. Leave it out to keep it.

purchasedAt.description: When it was bought, as the receipt says. Leave it out to keep it. An ISO 8601 date and time with its UTC offset, such as 2026-10-01T08:00:00-05:00.

quantity.description: The quantity bought, as a decimal such as 100.5, in quantityUnit. Leave it out to keep it.

quantityUnit.description: The unit the quantity is in. Defaults to Gallon. Leave it out to keep it.

taxPaid.description: Whether fuel tax was paid at the pump. Defaults to true; bulk or untaxed fuel earns no tax-paid credit. Leave it out to keep it.

totalAmount.description: The total paid as a decimal such as 389.90. Leave it out to keep it.

tractorId.description: The tractor the fuel went into, from list_tractors. Leave it out to keep it.

transactionReference.description: The receipt or transaction number; a purchase with a reference already on file is refused. Leave it out to keep it.

unitPrice.description: The price per unit as a decimal such as 3.899. Leave it out to keep it.

vendor.description: The truck stop or vendor. Leave it out to keep it.

vendorCity.description: The vendor's city. Leave it out to keep it.

workerId.description: The driver who bought it, from search_worker or list_workers. Leave it out to take the card's driver. Leave it out to keep it.

policy.taintHold: A purchase read from a receipt or statement someone outside sent is proposed, since it is a tax record the IFTA return is computed from.
policy.rationale: Changes a fuel purchase inside Trenova; nothing is sent, and a later correction changes it back.

tools.name: correct_ifta_mileage_entry
tools.description: Correct a jurisdiction mileage entry that was keyed wrong: its tractor, state or province, day, miles or notes. Fields left out keep their value. A finalized return keeps its figures until it is reopened or amended.

iftaMileageEntryId.description: The mileage entry, from list_ifta_mileage_entries. Never guess one.

jurisdictionId.description: The state or province the miles were driven in, from list_ifta_jurisdictions. Leave it out to keep it.

loaded.description: Whether the tractor was loaded. Defaults to true. Leave it out to keep it.

miles.description: The miles as a decimal such as 212.5. Leave it out to keep it.

notes.description: Where the miles came from, such as a trip sheet. Leave it out to keep it.

shipmentMoveId.description: The move these miles correct, from get_shipment; the entry then replaces the move's routed miles on the return. Leave it out to keep it.

tractorId.description: The tractor that drove the miles, from list_tractors. Leave it out to keep it.

traveledAt.description: When the miles were driven; it decides the quarter they count in. Leave it out to keep it. An ISO 8601 date and time with its UTC offset, such as 2026-10-01T08:00:00-05:00.

policy.taintHold: Miles read from a log or a message someone outside sent are proposed, since the IFTA return is computed from them.
policy.rationale: Changes jurisdiction miles inside Trenova; nothing is sent, and a later correction changes them back.

tools.name: create_accounting_reference_record
tools.description: Create an item, customer or vendor in the accounting system and map a Trenova record to it. Use it for an accessorial charge, line type, customer or carrier with no match there, and only when get_accounting_mapping's search finds no existing record; a duplicate is refused and names the existing one. Accounts, terms and payment methods are the bookkeeper's and are never created.

key.description: The setting's key from list_accounting_mapping_gaps, for the other target types. Examples: "ARAccount", "Freight", "Net30", "ACH".

mappingId.description: The mapping's id from list_accounting_mapping_gaps or get_accounting_mapping. Never guess one.

name.description: The name to create it under. Defaults to the Trenova record's name.

recordId.description: The Trenova customer, carrier or accessorial charge id, from list_customers, list_carriers or list_accessorial_charges.

targetType.description: The kind of Trenova record or setting, when naming it by recordId or key.

policy.rationale: Creates a record in the organization's own accounting system; Trenova cannot delete it again, so a person approves it.

tools.name: create_carrier
tools.description: Add a carrier the organization can tender freight to: its code, name, USDOT and MC numbers, SCAC, address and dispatch contact. Check list_carriers first. Vetting and compliance are vet_carrier's; payment and remit-to details are only proposed.

carrierType.description: What kind of carrier it is. Defaults to Common.

code.description: The carrier's short code, unique in this organization.

dbaName.description: The name it does business as, when that differs.

is1099Eligible.description: Whether payments are reported on a 1099.

mcNumber.description: The MC docket number, digits only.

name.description: The carrier's legal name.

notes.description: Anything colleagues booking this carrier should know.

paymentMethod.description: How the carrier is paid. Defaults to Check. Payment details are only ever proposed and change on a person's approval.

paymentTermDays.description: Days after the invoice the carrier is paid. Defaults to 30.

remitState.description: The remit-to state. The two-letter US state abbreviation, such as TX.

remitToName.description: Who payment is made out to.

scac.description: The two to four letter SCAC.

state.description: The state of the street address. The two-letter US state abbreviation, such as TX.

taxId.description: The tax id payments are reported under.

taxIdType.description: Whether the tax id is an EIN or an SSN; required with a tax id.

w9OnFile.description: Whether a signed W-9 is on file.

policy.taintHold: A record read from a document or message someone outside sent is proposed, since colleagues book and pay against it.
policy.rationale: Adds a carrier inside Trenova that colleagues can then book; nothing is sent. Payment and remit-to details decide where money goes, so a call that sets them is money and runs only on a person's approval.

tools.name: create_carrier_invoice_match
tools.description: Match a carrier's EDI invoice to the load it bills, comparing its total with what the carrier assignment was expected to cost. The match is Matched when within tolerance and Variance when not. Link the invoice to a carrier first with link_edi_carrier_invoice_to_carrier when it has none.

ediCarrierInvoiceId.description: The EDI carrier invoice, from list_edi_carrier_invoices. Never guess one.

proNumber.description: The pro number it bills, when the invoice carries none.

shipmentId.description: The shipment it bills, from search_shipments, when the invoice's own references do not find it.

policy.rationale: Records how a carrier's invoice compares with the expected cost inside Trenova; nothing is paid until a person accepts it.

tools.name: create_commodity
tools.description: Add a commodity shipments can carry, with its freight class, temperature range, dimensions and handling. Name the hazardous material it is when it is hazmat, and check list_commodities first.

description.description: What the goods are.

hazardousMaterialId.description: The hazardous material it is, from list_hazardous_materials, when the goods are hazmat.

heightPerUnit.description: Inches high per unit. A decimal such as 42.5.

lengthPerUnit.description: Inches long per unit. A decimal such as 42.5.

linearFeetPerUnit.description: Linear feet of trailer per unit. A decimal such as 42.5.

loadingInstructions.description: How it is loaded and secured.

maxQuantityPerShipment.description: The most units one shipment may carry. A decimal such as 42.5.

maxTemperature.description: The highest temperature it may be carried at, in degrees Fahrenheit.

minTemperature.description: The lowest temperature it may be carried at, in degrees Fahrenheit.

name.description: The commodity's name, unique in this organization.

weightPerUnit.description: Pounds per unit. A decimal such as 42.5.

widthPerUnit.description: Inches wide per unit. A decimal such as 42.5.

policy.taintHold: A record read from a document or message someone outside sent is proposed, since colleagues book and pay against it.
policy.rationale: Adds a commodity inside Trenova that shipments can name; nothing is sent and it can be made inactive.

tools.name: create_customer
tools.description: Add a customer the organization ships for: its code, name, billing address and DOT and MC numbers. Check list_customers first. Billing terms start from the organization's defaults; who is emailed status updates is only proposed.

allowConsolidation.description: Whether its shipments may be consolidated.

code.description: The customer's short code, unique in this organization.

consolidationPriority.description: Its priority when shipments are consolidated, 1 first.

dotNumber.description: The USDOT number, digits only, for a broker customer.

exclusiveConsolidation.description: Whether its shipments are consolidated only with each other; needs allowConsolidation.

mcNumber.description: The MC docket number, digits only.

name.description: The customer's name.

state.description: The state. The two-letter US state abbreviation, such as TX.

statusUpdatePreference.description: Which stop events the customer is emailed about. None stops the emails and clears the recipients. Changing who is emailed is only ever proposed.

statusUpdateRecipients.description: The addresses status updates go to, separated by commas.

policy.taintHold: A record read from a document or message someone outside sent is proposed, since colleagues book and pay against it.
policy.rationale: Adds a customer inside Trenova that shipments can be booked for; nothing is sent. Setting who receives status emails decides where later emails go, so that call is held for a person.

tools.name: create_dashboard
tools.description: Create a report dashboard: a page of saved or built-in reports under Reports. Use it when a person describes a screen of reports they want, such as "this week's revenue, on-time percentage and the unbilled backlog". Find each tile's report with list_reports first; never invent an id. Tiles are laid out for you. For a dashboard about a measure, lead with its headline figures as kpi tiles when the report has a column for them, then the detail table. Not for the person's home page — get_my_home_layout and add_home_widget are for that.

category.description: Optional grouping on the dashboards page, such as Operations.

description.description: One line on what the dashboard is for.

name.description: What to call it.

shared.description: Whether everyone in the organization sees it. Defaults to false.

tiles.description: What the page shows, in reading order.

cannedKey.description: A built-in report's key, from list_reports. Give this or definitionId, not both.

chartId.description: Which of the report's charts, for a chart tile; describe_report lists them.

columnId.description: The output column a KPI tile reads; describe_report lists them.

definitionId.description: A saved report's id, from list_reports. Give this or cannedKey, not both.

height.description: Rows the tile spans. Defaults to a sensible height for the kind.

kind.description: table, chart or kpi draws a report; text shows words.

text.description: The words a text tile shows.

title.description: Heading shown on the tile. Defaults to the report's name.

width.description: How many of the 12 columns the tile spans. Defaults to a sensible width for the kind.

policy.rationale: Saves a report dashboard colleagues can open; nothing leaves the organization.

tools.name: create_hazardous_material
tools.description: Add a hazardous material commodities can name, with its hazard class, UN number and packing group. Give the shipping name, placarding and emergency contact as the DOT table does; check list_hazardous_materials first, and a person always approves it.

class.description: The DOT hazard class or division.

description.description: What the material is.

emergencyContact.description: Who to call in an emergency.

ergGuideNumber.description: The Emergency Response Guidebook guide number.

inhalationHazard.description: Whether it is a poison inhalation hazard.

isReportableQuantity.description: Whether it is a reportable quantity substance.

marinePollutant.description: Whether it is a marine pollutant.

name.description: The material's name, unique in this organization.

packingGroup.description: The packing group: I is great danger, III minor.

placardRequired.description: Whether a vehicle carrying it must be placarded.

properShippingName.description: The proper shipping name from the hazardous materials table.

quantityThreshold.description: The reportable quantity; required when isReportableQuantity.

specialProvisions.description: The special provision codes, separated by commas.

unNumber.description: The four-digit UN or NA number, without the prefix.

policy.taintHold: A record read from a document or message someone outside sent is proposed, since colleagues book and pay against it.
policy.rationale: Adds a hazardous material inside Trenova; nothing is sent. Its class, placarding and emergency contact decide what drivers carry and post, so a person checks every one against the DOT table before it is saved.

tools.name: create_invoice
tools.description: Propose drafting invoices for completed freight: an order's billable shipments as one grouped invoice, or shipments on their own. A split-billed shipment makes one draft per payer. Drafts are posted with post_invoice. A person always decides.

offCycleReason.description: Why this customer's freight is billed now rather than on their periodic statement. Required only for statement customers.

orderId.description: The order to bill as one grouped invoice, from get_order or get_shipment.

shipmentIds.description: The shipments to bill, from search_shipments or get_shipment. With orderId, only these of the order's shipments.

policy.rationale: Turns freight into receivables and takes it off the billing queue and any statement; only a person decides what is billed and when.

tools.name: create_invoice_memo
tools.description: Propose a draft credit or debit memo to a customer with no shipment behind it, such as a goodwill credit or a returned-check fee. It stays a draft until post_invoice posts it; apply a posted credit with apply_credit_memo. A person always decides.

billType.description: CreditMemo lowers what the customer owes; DebitMemo raises it.

customerId.description: The customer, from list_customers or get_invoice.

invoiceDate.description: The memo's date; defaults to today. YYYY-MM-DD, a UTC day.

lines.description: The memo's lines, each a positive amount.

accessorialChargeId.description: The accessorial the line corrects, from get_invoice's lines.

amount.description: The line's unit amount in major units, such as 125.00.

description.description: What the line is for.

memo.description: A note printed on the memo.

reason.description: Why the memo is raised; the customer sees it.

referenceInvoiceId.description: The posted invoice this memo relates to, from list_invoices or get_invoice.

policy.rationale: Raises what a customer owes or is owed outside any shipment; only a person decides it, and it is never posted as it is made.

tools.name: create_location
